gloss: firstly; first of all; in the first place

definitions.gloss: firstly; first of all; in the first place
definitions.explanation: Used to introduce the first point in a series of arguments or reasons. Also used to emphasize that something is the most important consideration.

examples.japanese: {第一|だいいち}に、{安全|あんぜん}を{確認|かくにん}してください。
examples.english: First of all, please confirm safety.

examples.japanese: {第一|だいいち}に{健康|けんこう}、{第二|だいに}に{家族|かぞく}が{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: Health comes first, family comes second.

examples.japanese: この{計画|けいかく}には{問題|もんだい}がある。{第一|だいいち}に{予算|よさん}が{足|た}りない。
examples.english: There are problems with this plan. First of all, the budget is insufficient.

notes:
{第一|だいいち}に introduces the first and often most important point in a series. It is used in logical arguments, speeches, and essays.

SERIES PATTERN:
Often used with sequential markers:
- {第一|だいいち}に (firstly)
- {第二|だいに}に (secondly)
- {第三|だいさん}に (thirdly)

WITHOUT に:
{第一|だいいち} alone (without に) emphasizes priority: {健康|けんこう}{第一|だいいち} (health first), {安全|あんぜん}{第一|だいいち} (safety first).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- まず: first, to begin with (more colloquial and versatile)
- {最初|さいしょ}に: at first, initially (temporal focus)
- {何|なに}よりも: above all else (strongest emphasis on priority)
- そもそも: in the first place (challenges premises, more confrontational)

REGISTER:
Neutral to formal. Common in structured arguments and formal writing. In casual speech, まず is preferred.
